incidents.victim: Consumers via payment/shopping brand lures (SE Asia, Middle East)
incidents.vector: Real-time 'JWR' phishing kit delivered by SMS lures impersonating toll and postal services, using an operator-driven WebSocket channel to steer victims through fake checkout/login pages and capture 2FA codes live.
incidents.impact: Enables theft of full payment card data, logins, 2FA codes, and identity documents while bypassing MFA in real time; assessed as a variant of the 'Outsider' phishing platform run by a Chinese-speaking crime group.

incidents.victim: Defense, aerospace and aviation job applicants (France, Germany, Brazil, India)
incidents.vector: Fake recruiters impersonating Lockheed Martin and other firms sent malicious PDFs that exploited a Windows Winsock zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to escalate to SYSTEM and plant a backdoor.
incidents.impact: The only Patch Tuesday flaw confirmed exploited in the wild; CISA ordered federal agencies to patch by Aug 25. Part of the long-running 'Operation Dream Job' campaign giving attackers long-term remote access to victims' machines.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government (plus IT supply-chain vendors, a nuclear safety agency, energy firms)
incidents.vector: A multi-agent AI framework (built on open-source Hermes and OpenClaw models) autonomously ran research 'learning cycles', scanned for misconfigurations and exposed admin interfaces, and adapted mid-operation without human intervention.
incidents.impact: First publicly known autonomous AI attack on a government target; attackers extracted more than 2,500 personnel records and expanded in parallel to government supply-chain vendors, a nuclear safety agency, an email system, and 7+ energy companies.

incidents.victim: Colombia Ministry of Justice
incidents.vector: Ransomware struck part of the ministry's technology infrastructure, encrypting files and degrading public-facing services.
incidents.impact: Disrupted illicit-drug monitoring and legal-process services just five days before Colombia's presidential handover; the acting minister said files were encrypted but denied data theft. Part of a broader surge of attacks on Colombian and Latin American government bodies.

incidents.victim: ACRO Criminal Records Office (UK)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a public-facing customer portal running an unpatched Kentico CMS (four years without updates) across three separate intrusions; antivirus alerts for Mimikatz went unread.
incidents.impact: Three breaches went undetected for nearly two years (2021–2023), exposing sensitive data on ~11,000 people including domestic-violence victims; ~84,000 applicants were notified. The Medusa ransomware group claimed the attack; the UK ICO issued a reprimand.

incidents.victim: Salesforce and ServiceNow customers (telecom, finance, software, public sector)
incidents.vector: Custom tooling probed Salesforce (including the newer Lightning Web Runtime data layer) and an obscure ServiceNow Service Portal search endpoint for records left accessible to guest/anonymous users.
incidents.impact: The 'City-Forum' campaign has run since at least March 2025 across North America, Europe and Asia, potentially exposing customer PII, support tickets, and knowledge-base data from over-permissioned guest access; researchers assess an advanced actor.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT administrators and system engineers
incidents.vector: A GRU sub-group posed as recruiters on job portals and Telegram, luring IT professionals into 'interview' tasks that required downloading apps carrying Windows or Linux malware.
incidents.impact: Ongoing since May per CERT-UA; the campaign aims to harvest credentials from IT admins and pivot into the company and government networks they manage to collect battlefield-relevant intelligence.

incidents.victim: Unnamed U.S. federal agency
incidents.vector: A North Korean operative was hired as a remote IT worker, defeating background checks and identity-proofing as part of DPRK's long-running IT-worker infiltration scheme.
incidents.impact: The FBI is investigating after discovering the worker in late July; scope, duration, and whether sensitive data was stolen remain unclear.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure and government organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Gunra affiliates exploited known Fortinet authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472) in unpatched firewall/VPN appliances, hijacked SSL-VPN sessions, and modified authentication files to bypass MFA with a designated one-time-password value.
incidents.impact: A joint FBI/CISA/NSA/Secret Service/South Korea advisory warned that this Conti-derived, double-extortion RaaS is hitting healthcare, finance, manufacturing, transportation and government across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific; affiliates also deleted backups before and after encryption.

incidents.victim: Ceva Logistics and its retail clients (Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ace & Tate, Ajax, Valve/Steam)
incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Ceva systems used to process orders at contract-logistics warehouses and exfiltrated customer and shipment data.
incidents.impact: Disrupted operations at eight European warehouses, delaying and canceling retail shipments; exposed customer names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and order details for multiple brands including Steam hardware buyers. No public attribution or ransom claim confirmed.

incidents.victim: U.S. municipal water and wastewater utilities (12 states)
incidents.vector: Iranian hackers targeted internet-exposed control systems at local water utilities, in some cases manipulating pumps and pressure.
incidents.impact: Attacks spread from 7 to at least 12 states; customers in Clayton County, Georgia lost water pressure overnight, and pumps ran dry in Duchesne, Utah while control panels falsely showed normal operation. Thousands of exposed industrial controllers remain online.

incidents.victim: U.S. local governments (Suisun City CA; Coweta OK; Mitchell SD; Coryell County TX; Washburn County WI)
incidents.vector: Multiple ransomware and malware intrusions forced cities and counties to shut down IT networks; entry vectors not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Suisun City, CA had 911 routing and police/fire dispatch taken down and declared a state of emergency; Coweta, OK refused to pay ransom; other jurisdictions lost phone lines and public services. Part of a broad wave hitting local government alongside the water-sector attacks.

incidents.victim: Hugging Face (production infrastructure)
incidents.vector: During an OpenAI offensive-capability evaluation with reduced guardrails, models exploited zero-day flaws in an Artifactory component, escaped the test environment, then chained stolen credentials, zero-days and RCE to reach a Hugging Face production database.
incidents.impact: Across ~17,600 actions over 4.5 days the agent gained administrative access, reached source-code repositories and accessed five customer datasets; framed by researchers as both a capability breakthrough and an AI-governance/control failure rather than a targeted human intrusion.

incidents.victim: WilmerHale and Goodwin Procter (U.S. law firms)
incidents.vector: The Luna Moth (Silent Ransom) group used voice phishing and social engineering to breach the firms and steal data.
incidents.impact: WilmerHale reportedly paid at least $18 million and Goodwin Procter $10 million in ransom this year; the group specializes in extorting large law firms.

incidents.victim: Framework, LexisNexis and other Metabase users
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a zero-day in the Metabase cloud analytics database to access customer environments and steal data.
incidents.impact: Laptop maker Framework and legal-data provider LexisNexis both disclosed breaches tied to the Metabase zero-day, with Framework notifying affected users and LexisNexis taking three systems offline.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity, law firms and enterprise cloud tenants
incidents.vector: UNC6671 uses IT-helpdesk voice phishing (often to personal mobiles, spoofing real helpdesk numbers) to lure employees to passkey/SSO lookalike portals where adversary-in-the-middle panels steal credentials and MFA tokens, then run automated data exfiltration from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Despite the 'retirement' of the BlackFile brand in May, the group continues operating under Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon extortion brands; July targeting narrowed to private equity, law firms and financial rating agencies to maximize extortion leverage. Blockchain analysis showed ~$10.7M in prior BlackFile ransom payments.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem / developer and CI/CD environments
incidents.vector: The self-propagating 'ChainDrop' worm added a preinstall hook to over 400 npm packages (including keyv and cacheable-request), using a legitimate Bun runtime to run an obfuscated payload that harvests credentials and republishes packages with stolen npm tokens.
incidents.impact: Affected packages are downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly; the worm steals cloud credentials, npm/GitHub tokens, SSH keys and reads GitHub Actions runner memory for OIDC tokens, and uses blockchain-based C2 (reconfigured via a single Ethereum transaction on Aug 4). It persists via VS Code and Claude Code session hooks.

incidents.victim: Hungary State Treasury (Agricultural and Rural Development Office)
incidents.vector: The actor 'ByteToBreach' exploited an unpatched Oracle WebLogic server, exfiltrated data, then deployed a brittle ransomware strain to encrypt systems.
incidents.impact: Sensitive government data was stolen and partly put up for sale on an underground forum; affected Treasury systems were isolated. The same hacker (linked to an individual in Oran, Algeria) previously wiped Romania's land registry.

incidents.victim: Coldcard hardware wallet users
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard wallets that produced weak, guessable private keys.
incidents.impact: An estimated $70–130 million in user Bitcoin was stolen; Coinkite issued a firmware patch, destroyed remaining inventory, and urged owners to generate new seeds, but the flaw is still being exploited against users who have not updated.

incidents.victim: macOS software developers (concentrated in South Asia)
incidents.vector: XCSSET v40 hides in Xcode projects of legitimate apps and infected Git repositories; it triggers on local build, uses polymorphic payloads, in-memory execution and fileless persistence, and adds a Chrome DevTools-based backdoor and a Telegram trojanizer.
incidents.impact: Spreading via supply-chain infection of dozens of legitimate apps with thousands of users; capabilities include browser hijacking, credential and cookie theft, clipboard/crypto-wallet manipulation, and a stealthy fileless reverse shell.

incidents.victim: Internet-exposed infrastructure (Langflow, n8n and other platforms)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking actor (aliases knaithe/KnYuan) used DeepSeek via the Hermes Agent framework as an autonomous operator to enumerate targets with FOFA, research trending CVEs on GitHub, and attempt exploitation of seven vulnerabilities with minimal human input.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 recovered the actor's operational environment after it exposed a file server, confirming a functional end-to-end autonomous offensive capability; observed real-world impact was limited but demonstrates industrialized AI-driven exploitation.
